claims.text: The initial TiVNbTa alloy is a single-phase BCC alloy with a dendritic microstructure.
The baseline TiVNbTa alloy has a yield strength of approximately 330 MPa at 1273 K.
The baseline TiVNbTa alloy has a compressive strength of approximately 423 MPa at 30% strain and 1273 K.
A minor carbon addition during synthesis will promote in-situ formation of MC carbide precipitates in TiVNbTa.
The carbon-induced MC precipitates will be nanoscale, uniformly dispersed, and thermally stable in the BCC matrix.
Precipitation strengthening can improve the elevated-temperature strength of HEAs.
Finely dispersed MC carbides will impede dislocation motion at elevated temperature.
Finely dispersed MC carbides will impede grain-boundary sliding at elevated temperature.
Carbon-induced MC precipitation will increase the high-temperature yield and compressive strength of TiVNbTa relative to the baseline.
The modified alloy can attain a yield strength greater than 500 MPa at approximately 1273 K.
The modified alloy will maintain acceptable ductility and compressive performance.
The carbon-modified alloy can remain compatible with service as a thermal and structural interface between W and CuCrZr.
The proposed performance must be sustained at temperatures up to approximately 1273 K.
The proposed performance is to be evaluated under deformation reaching 30–40% strain.
Single-phase HEAs can have insufficient strength at elevated temperatures.
Precipitates have produced moderate tensile-strength increases in CoCrFeNiNbx and CoCrFeNiMox HEAs.
Grain refinement and precipitation strengthening improved mechanical strength in mechanically alloyed and spark-plasma-sintered NbMoTaWVTi.
An increase of less than approximately 50 MPa over the 330 MPa baseline, or failure to obtain uniformly distributed nanoscale MC precipitates, is defined as a falsifying result.
